newsitem.title: USA: Judge refuses to block Healthdyne poison pill.
newsitem.headline: Judge refuses to block Healthdyne poison pill.

text.p: A federal judge Thursday denied a request by Invacare Corp. to overturn part of hostile target Healthdyne Technologies Inc.'s shareholder rights plan, or "poison pill."

In a 13-page decision, Judge Clarence Cooper in Atlanta ruled that medical equipment manufacturer Invacare had failed to prove it would suffer irreparable harm if the preliminary injunction it sought was not issued.
Invacare has launched a $200 million hostile bid for Marietta, Ga.-based Healthdyne, which makes advanced medical devices.
Elyria, Ohio-based Invacare had sought the preliminary injunction to invalidate the portion of the pill known as a "continuing directors," or "deadhand" provision.

The provision essentially prohibits a new slate of directors from overturning Healthdyne's poison pill, which makes it prohibitively expensive for an investor to amass more than 5 percent of the company.
Invacare, which argued that the Healthdyne provision is illegal, has launched a proxy fight to install its own directors in order to take control of the company and abolish the poision pill.
In his ruling, Cooper noted that Georgia corporate law has supported the concept of continuing directors as a defence strategy against hostile takeovers.
"... The court is satisfied that the concept of continuing directors is an integral part of a takeover defence and is not contrary to public policy in Georgia," he wrote.

Cooper also denied Invacare's attempt to propose a bylaw that would require the Healthdyne board to eliminate the continuing directors provision. Invacare had wanted shareholders to vote on the bylaw at the July 30 annual meeting.
"Needless to say, we are very pleased with the decision," Healthdyne Chief Executive Officer Craig Reynolds said in a telephone interview.
Invacare Chief Executive Officer Malachi Mixon said the company will probably appeal the decision.
Healthdyne stock closed down 50 cents at $16.625 and Invacare closed unchanged at $23.125, both on Nasdaq.
